fact_text: Silver rose about 140 percent in 2025, from about USD 29 an ounce on 1 January 2025 to about USD 70 an ounce, the guest said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: Silver was about USD 37 an ounce on 1 August 2025 and climbed sharply after July, reaching about USD 70 later in the year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: Gold rose about 70 percent in 2025, from about USD 2,625 an ounce at the start of the year to about USD 4,500.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The US dollar fell about 10 percent against a basket of currencies in 2025, which the guest linked to investor interest in tangible assets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: Gold rose from about USD 35 an ounce in 1971 to about USD 850 by 20 January 1980, an increase of about 2,328 percent over nine years that the guest used as an analogue for 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The guest said most global central banks began adding gold after 2022, following the same pattern seen when central banks bought gold from 1976 to 1982.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: Investors facing inflation and geopolitical risk moved toward tangible assets such as gold, silver, real estate, farmland and vineyards, as the guest said happened in the 1970s.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The guest said silver mining output has not kept pace with demand, which drove the price up and was expected to keep it rising.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The guest cited industrial demand for silver from electric vehicles and data centres, which also use copper, as a driver of the silver rally.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The guest cited about 11,000 data centres worldwide as a growing source of silver and copper demand.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: Forecasts from Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and UBS, as cited in the video, put gold at about USD 5,000 an ounce by December 2026.

fact_text: The guest, global chief economist at IQI, expects gold to reach about USD 6,000 an ounce, around 30 percent above the USD 4,500 level at recording.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The guest said silver could reach about USD 150 an ounce, roughly double the USD 70 level, and that a correction is possible along the way.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Why Silver Was 2025's Top-Performing Asset | How to Money | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-26)

fact_text: The guest cautioned that commodity prices do not rise in a straight line, with profit taking and corrections normal, so investors should learn an asset class before investing.
